Return a list of triplets containing current level, next level threshold, and progress percentage. Example: a player at the exact threshold for level two shows zero percent progress toward level three.

title: Text histogram generator
spec: Create a vertical ASCII bar chart showing letter frequencies using `histogram(text, width)`. The logic must count alphabetical characters in the text while ignoring case, and find the highest frequency to determine a proportional scaling factor based on the given maximum width and height. It must build horizontal rows of hash characters and spaces from top to bottom to visually represent the distribution. Return a single multi-line string containing the rendered chart. Example: a text heavily featuring the letter E will show a tall column of hashes above the letter E label.

title: Email address parser
spec: Extract routing components from a list of complex formatted email strings using `parse(emails)`. The logic must process each string to isolate the display name if present before the angle brackets. It must split the remaining address at the at symbol to separate the local part and domain, and check for any plus suffix in the local part to extract subaddress tags. Return a list of lists containing the display name, base local part, tag, and domain for each email. Example: Jane Doe angle bracket jane dot doe plus newsletter at example dot com yields four distinct string components.

title: Word search puzzle solver
spec: Locate a list of target words hidden within a grid of letters using `search(grid, words)`. The logic must scan the two dimensional grid for the starting letter of each word and check all eight compass directions for the remaining sequence without wrapping around the board edges. It must record the successful starting row, column, and directional heading for every discovered word. Return a list of lists containing the word, starting coordinates, and compass direction. Example: finding the word cat reading horizontally backwards yields the start position and West direction.

title: Version number comparator
spec: Sort a list of semantic version strings from oldest to newest using `order(versions)`. The logic must parse each string by splitting it into major, minor, and patch integers. It must correctly handle optional pre-release identifiers appended with a hyphen, prioritizing numerical comparisons over alphabetical string comparisons so that a patch of ten is evaluated as greater than two. Return the fully sorted list of version strings. Example: version one dot two is sorted before version one dot ten.

title: Polyline decimation
spec: Reduce the number of points in a segmented path while retaining its geometric shape using `simplify(points, tolerance)`. The logic implements a recursive distance threshold by finding the point furthest from the straight line segment connecting the first and last points of a sequence. If this maximum perpendicular distance exceeds the given tolerance, it must recursively split the path at this furthest point and process both halves. Return the filtered list of remaining coordinate pairs. Example: a straight line defined by ten collinear points is decimated down to just its two endpoints.

title: Euclidean rhythm generator
spec: Distribute a given number of active beats evenly across a sequence of timing steps using `rhythm(pulses, steps)`. The logic must initialize groups of active beats and empty beats as separate lists. It must repeatedly pair the largest sequence groups to interleave them, progressively reducing the number of leftover sequences, and finally flatten the nested structure into a single binary rhythm sequence. Return a list of ones and zeroes. Example: three pulses distributed over eight steps produces a pattern of one, zero, zero, one, zero, zero, one, zero.

title: String inflector
spec: Convert a list of singular English nouns into their correct plural forms using `pluralize(words)`. The logic must process each word by checking it against a small predefined dictionary of irregular nouns like child to children. If not irregular, it must apply suffix rules for words ending in s, x, z, or ch by adding es, change a trailing consonant followed by y to ies, and simply append s as the default fallback rule. Return a list of pluralized strings. Example: box becomes boxes and city becomes cities.

title: Train ticket routing
spec: Reconstruct a continuous travel itinerary from an unordered list of boarding passes using `route(tickets)`. Each ticket contains an origin and destination city. The logic must identify the true starting city by finding the origin that never appears as a destination in any pass. It must iteratively search for the connecting ticket to the next destination to chain the legs of the journey together, building the entire sequence of stops. Return a list of city names in order of travel. Example: disjointed passes from Paris to Berlin and London to Paris yield a combined itinerary of London, Paris, Berlin.

title: Checkers move validator
spec: Determine if a proposed sequence of squares on an eight by eight board constitutes a legal checkers move using `validate(board, move)`. The logic must verify that the piece at the starting square belongs to the active player. It must check that each consecutive step to a destination square is diagonally forward unless the piece is a king, and ensure any multi-step jump sequence correctly lands on empty squares while effectively passing over opponent pieces. Return a boolean indicating if the entire path is valid. Example: attempting to move a regular piece straight forward returns false.

title: Ski jumping scorer
spec: Calculate the final event scores for a list of ski jumps using `judge(jumps, kpoint)`. Each jump contains a landing distance and five style scores from the judge panel. The logic must compute distance points by adding or subtracting from a base of sixty depending on the jumper's relation to the critical point. It must then discard the highest and lowest style scores, summing the remaining three and adding them to the distance points. Return a list of total numeric scores for all jumps. Example: landing exactly on the critical point with all judges awarding twenties gives a total of one hundred and twenty points.

title: Sailing race handicap scoring
spec: Function `score(races)`. A sailing regatta records start time, finish time, and a boat handicap rating. You must process a list of plain strings with boat name, rating, start time, and finish time separated by commas. Extract the details, calculate the elapsed time in seconds, apply the time correction factor by multiplying elapsed time by the rating, and rank the boats. Output a list of strings ranking the boats by corrected time. Times are given in hours, minutes, and seconds separated by colons. Example input: Alpha, 0.95, 12:00:00, 13:15:30. Example output: Alpha: 4303 seconds.

title: Bicycle gear ratio calculator
spec: Function `analyze(drivetrain)`. Calculates the distance a bicycle travels per pedal stroke based on chainring size, cog size, and wheel circumference in millimeters. Input is an array of strings such as Front 50, Rear 15, Wheel 2100. You must extract the teeth counts and wheel size, compute the gear ratio by dividing front by rear, multiply by wheel circumference to get rollout in meters, and categorize it as climbing for under four meters, flat for four to seven meters, or sprint for over seven meters. Output an array of sentences stating the ratio, rollout, and category. Example: Front 50, Rear 15, Wheel 2100 becomes Ratio 3.33, Rollout 6.99 meters, flat.

title: Beehive honey yield forecaster
spec: Function `forecast(hives)`. Predicts total honey production based on apiary inspections. Input strings contain hive name, bee count, frame count, and weather condition separated by commas. Each ten thousand bees gather a baseline of five units of nectar. Frames determine storage capacity, where each frame holds ten units. Weather applies a multiplier: excellent adds twenty percent, poor subtracts thirty percent. You must extract the numbers, calculate base gathering, apply weather multipliers, cap by frame capacity, and convert nectar to honey where yield is eighty percent of nectar. Return a list of forecast sentences. Example input: HiveA, 50000, 15, excellent. Example output: HiveA will produce 24 units of honey.

title: Drone flight path energy consumption
spec: Function `simulate(maneuvers)`. Evaluates if a drone can complete a flight plan on a single battery charge. Input is an array of commands like Hover 5 minutes, Fly 2000 meters, Climb 100 meters. Parse each command to compute energy drained based on activity. Hovering takes ten units per minute, flying takes two units per meter, climbing takes fifty units per meter. Subtract these from a starting battery capacity of ten thousand units and check if it drops below zero. Output a list of battery levels after each step, or a failure message if depleted. Example: Hover 2 minutes leaves 9980 units remaining.

title: Aquarium water quality analyzer
spec: Function `evaluate(readings)`. Processes daily water test results. Input strings format is day number, pH, ammonia, and nitrate separated by commas. Extract the values and check if pH is outside the safe range of six point eight to seven point six, if ammonia exceeds zero point two, and if nitrate exceeds forty. Calculate a water health score starting at one hundred, deducting five points for each parameter out of bounds. Output an array of action strings for days needing attention, stating the day and the specific parameters that failed. Example input: Day 1, 7.2, 0.5, 20. Example output: Day 1: high ammonia.

title: Historical timeline merger
spec: Function `merge(periods)`. Takes a list of historical empires and their start and end years, and finds the total number of unique years covered across all of them. Parse the input strings which contain the name, start year, and end year separated by commas. Represent the periods as ranges, sort them by start year, merge overlapping periods to avoid double counting, and sum the total duration. Output the total span of years as a single number. Example input: Roman, -27, 476 and Han, -202, 220. Example output: 678.

title: Wind turbine power output estimator
spec: Function `estimate(conditions)`. Calculates generated electricity based on hourly wind speed logs. Input is a list of strings stating the hour and wind speed in meters per second. Parse the wind speed for each hour. If speed is below the cut in of three meters per second, output is zero. Between three and twelve, power equals speed cubed times a constant of two. Above twelve up to twenty five, output is capped at three thousand. Above twenty five, the turbine shuts down for safety producing zero. Output the total daily power generated. Example input: Hour 1, 8. Output would include 1024 for that hour.

title: Knitting pattern stitch counter
spec: Function `tally(rows)`. Calculates the total number of stitches and required yarn length for a knitting project. Input consists of pattern instructions like Knit 10, Purl 5, Repeat 3 times. Parse the command to find the base stitches for one sequence, multiply by the repeat count, and calculate yarn length where each knit takes three centimeters and each purl takes four centimeters. Output a sentence with the total stitches and total meters of yarn needed. Example input: Knit 10, Purl 5, Repeat 2 times. Output: 30 stitches, 1 meter of yarn.

title: Smart home power consumption monitor
spec: Function `aggregate(appliances)`. Calculates the monthly electricity cost from appliance usage logs. Input strings contain appliance name, wattage, and daily usage hours separated by commas. Extract the wattage and daily hours to compute daily kilowatt hours. Multiply by thirty for the monthly usage. Apply a tiered electricity rate where the first hundred kilowatt hours cost ten cents each, and any remainder costs twenty cents each. Output a list of appliance monthly costs and the total bill at the end. Example input: Heater, 1500, 4. Cost for this is 180 kilowatt hours, which is 26 dollars.

title: Plant watering schedule generator
spec: Function `schedule(plants)`. Determines the next watering day for indoor plants. Input strings list the plant name, last watered day, current moisture level, and required moisture level. Parse the plant data and evaluate current moisture against required moisture. Calculate how many days until the next watering based on the gap: if current matches required, water in three days; if current is one level below required, water in one day; if more than one level below, water immediately. Moisture levels from low to high are bone dry, dry, moist, wet. Output a list of actions for each plant. Example input: Fern, Monday, dry, moist. Output: Fern: water in 1 day.

title: Gemstone facet cutting planner
spec: Function `plan(stones)`. Determines the number of facets and expected yield for rough gemstones. Input strings contain gemstone type, rough weight in carats, and desired cut style. Parse the gemstone type, weight, and cut. Calculate expected final weight by applying a cut specific waste factor where round loses fifty percent and princess loses forty percent. Determine the facet count based on the cut style, which is fifty seven for round and fifty eight for princess. Output a list of sentences detailing the finished stone weight and facet count. Example input: Diamond, 10, round. Output: Diamond: 5 carats, 57 facets.

title: Orchestra seating arranger
spec: Function `arrange(musicians)`. Assigns seats to orchestra members based on their instrument and rank. Input strings contain the musician name, instrument, and rank separated by commas. Parse the musician details to assign them to a stage section. Strings sit in the front section, woodwinds in the middle, and brass in the rear. Determine their row within the section based on rank, where principal players get the first row and tutti players get the second row. Output a seating chart list with their name and assigned location. Example input: John, Violin, Principal. Output: John: front section, first row.

title: Railway ticket fare calculator
spec: Function `fare(trips)`. Calculates ticket prices based on origin and destination transit zones. Input strings contain origin zone, destination zone, and passenger type. Parse the zones, which are lettered A through E. Calculate the base fare by counting the number of zone boundaries crossed at three dollars per boundary, plus a base boarding fee of two dollars. Apply passenger discounts where seniors get fifty percent off and students get twenty five percent off. Add a five percent station tax to the final amount. Output an array of formatted fare strings. Example input: Zone A, Zone C, Senior. Output: Final fare: 4.20.

title: Book indexing engine
spec: Function `index(pages)`. Generates a keyword index for a manuscript. Input is an array of strings representing pages, where the first word is the page number and the rest is the text. Extract the page number, clean the text by removing punctuation and converting to lowercase, and filter out common stop words like the, and, or. Find all unique remaining words on that page and build an alphabetical index mapping each word to a list of pages it appears on. Output a list of formatted index entries. Example input: 1 the quick brown fox. Output: brown: 1, fox: 1, quick: 1.

title: Brewery fermentation monitor
spec: Function `monitor(readings)`. Tracks beer fermentation progress. Input strings contain the day number, temperature in Celsius, and specific gravity. Extract the day, temperature, and specific gravity. Determine the fermentation phase: if gravity drops by more than zero point zero one from the previous day, it is active; if less, it is conditioning; if stable for two consecutive days, it is finished. Check if temperature is outside the optimal ale range of eighteen to twenty two degrees. Output a status report for each day. Example input: Day 3, 20, 1.050. Output: Day 3: active, temperature normal.

title: Radio station playlist generator
spec: Function `compile(tracks)`. Builds an hour long broadcast from a pool of songs. Input strings contain the song name, genre, and duration in minutes. Parse the track details and select songs sequentially to fill exactly sixty minutes. A rule requires that you alternate genres so a rock song cannot immediately follow a rock song. You must also insert a two minute commercial break after every fifteen minutes of music. Output the final ordered list of songs and commercials. Example input: Song A, Rock, 4 and Song B, Pop, 3. Example output: Song A, Song B, Commercial.

title: Board game resource trader
spec: Function `trade(actions)`. Resolves marketplace trades in a resource gathering game. Input strings format is player name, amount offered, resource offered, amount requested, and resource requested. Parse these details and verify if the trade meets the bank exchange rate. The standard bank rate is four identical resources for one of any other. If they are trading grain, a special port rate allows trading two grain for one of any other. If the trade is valid, calculate the new quantities. Output a list of strings showing the approved trades and rejected trades. Example input: Player 1, 4 wood, 1 brick. Output: Player 1 trade approved.

title: Telescope observation scheduler
spec: Function `allocate(targets)`. Schedules night sky viewing sessions. Input strings contain the target name, required duration in minutes, and priority level. Parse the target, duration, and priority. Sort targets first by priority with high first, then medium, then low, and then by duration from shortest to longest. Allocate them sequentially into a limited viewing window of two hundred forty minutes. Skip any target that does not fit in the remaining time. Output a schedule list showing the start time in minutes from zero and the target name. Example input: Mars, 30, high. Output: 0: Mars.

title: Forestry timber yield estimator
spec: Function `compute(trees)`. Calculates the usable lumber from a plot of trees. Input strings contain the tree species, trunk diameter in centimeters, and height in meters. Parse the species, diameter, and height. Calculate the trunk volume assuming a perfect cylinder shape. Subtract twenty percent from the volume to account for bark and processing waste. Apply a wood density multiplier based on species, where oak is one point two and pine is zero point nine, to calculate total board feet of lumber. Output the total volume across all trees and a list of yields per tree. Example input: Pine, 40, 15. Output: Pine: 1.35 board feet.

title: Ski resort lift network status
spec: Function `status(reports)`. Determines which ski lifts can safely operate based on weather station telemetry. Input strings contain the lift name, wind speed in kilometers per hour, and recent snowfall in centimeters. Parse the lift name, wind speed, and snowfall. A lift must close if wind exceeds sixty. If snowfall is over fifty, it must be put on avalanche hold. If wind is between forty and sixty, it operates on reduced speed. Otherwise, it is fully open. Output an array of status strings for each lift. Example input: Summit Lift, 45, 20. Output: Summit Lift: reduced speed.

title: Amusement park ride queue simulator
spec: Function `predict(rides)`. Calculates the estimated wait time for amusement park rides based on line length and dispatch rate. Input strings contain the ride name, current queue size in persons, capacity per dispatch, and dispatch interval in minutes. Parse the ride name, current queue size, capacity, and interval. Calculate how many people exit the line per minute by dividing capacity by the interval. Divide the total queue by this throughput to get the wait time in minutes, rounding to the nearest integer. Output an array of wait time announcements. Example input: Rollercoaster, 500, 24, 3. Output: Rollercoaster wait is 63 minutes.

title: Wildlife tracker migration analyzer
spec: Function `track(logs)`. Identifies resting periods during a bird migration from GPS daily logs. Input strings contain the day number and daily distance traveled in kilometers. Parse the day and distance. Calculate a rolling average of the distance over the current and two previous days. If the daily distance drops below twenty kilometers and the rolling average is also below fifty kilometers, flag that day as a resting stop. Output a summary of the total distance traveled and a list of the days identified as rest stops. Example input: Day 3, 15. Output: Day 3 flagged as rest.

title: Coffee roasting profile analyzer
spec: Function `inspect(profiles)`. Evaluates temperature logs to ensure quality coffee roasting. Input strings contain minute mark, temperature in Celsius, and bean color. Parse the minute, temperature, and color. A roast is flagged with a warning if the temperature rises by more than twenty degrees in a single minute, or if it exceeds two hundred twenty degrees. The first crack phase must occur between minute eight and ten, indicated by a temperature over one hundred ninety and a color of light brown. Determine if the roast meets all quality standards or list the warnings. Output a summary report of warnings or a success message. Example input: Minute 8, 195, light brown. Output: Roast successful.

title: Bakery dough proofing timer
spec: Function `calculate(batches)`. Determines how long bread dough needs to rise based on kitchen conditions. Input strings contain the bread type, room temperature in Celsius, and humidity percentage. Parse the bread type, temperature, and humidity. Calculate the base proofing time, which is four hours for sourdough and two hours for commercial yeast. Adjust for temperature by subtracting ten minutes for every degree above twenty, or adding fifteen minutes for every degree below. If humidity is above seventy percent, reduce the final time by ten percent. Output the final proofing time in minutes. Example input: Sourdough, 22, 60. Output: 220 minutes.

title: Postal route delivery sequencer
spec: Function `sequence(packages)`. Optimizes the order of package deliveries on a single street. Input strings contain the house number and delivery priority level. Parse the house number and priority, which can be express or standard. Sort the packages first by priority, placing express before standard, and then by house number in ascending order within each group. Calculate the total distance walked to deliver all packages in this sorted order, assuming the postman starts at house zero and each house number increment represents ten meters of walking. Output the sorted delivery list and total distance. Example input: House 12, express. Output: Distance: 120 meters.

title: Restaurant health inspection score
spec: Implement `evaluate(inspections)` to process a list of health inspection records. Each record is a list containing the restaurant name, a list of violation codes, and the days since the last inspection. The logic must translate violation codes into penalty points: critical violations add five points, and minor ones add one point. It must also flag a restaurant for immediate closure if it has more than three critical violations or if the total penalty points exceed twenty. Return a list of sentences for each restaurant stating its name, total penalty points, and whether it passed or requires closure.

title: Soccer league standings generator
spec: Implement `standings(matches)` which takes a list of game results. Each result is a text string featuring two team names and their respective goals separated by a colon, such as falcons two eagles zero. The logic must parse the text to extract the team names and their goals. It then assigns three points for a win, one for a tie, and zero for a loss, while also tracking the difference between goals scored and conceded. Finally, sort the teams highest points first, using goal difference to break ties, and return an ordered list of team names.

title: Podcast episode silence trimmer
spec: Write a function `trim(audio)` that accepts a list of volume levels recorded every second in a podcast. The logic must identify continuous blocks of silence, defined as a volume level of zero lasting longer than three consecutive seconds. For each silence block, calculate the removable duration by keeping only the first and last second of the block for a natural pause. Accumulate the total seconds saved across the entire episode and return a formatted sentence stating the original duration, the new duration, and the total seconds removed.

title: Warehouse pallet stacking validator
spec: Create `validate(pallets)` to process a list of pallet items to be stacked on a forklift. Each item is a list containing the item identifier, its weight in kilograms, and a fragility category of fragile or sturdy. The logic must confirm that no fragile item is placed beneath a sturdy item in the list order. It must also verify that the cumulative weight does not exceed the forklift maximum capacity of two thousand kilograms. Return a list of accepted item identifiers up to the point of a rule violation, or all identifiers if the stack is perfectly valid.

title: Subscription tier feature access
spec: Implement `access(requests)` to process user attempts to use premium application features. Each request is a list with the user name, their current subscription tier of basic or premium, and the requested feature name. The logic must check if the tier allows the feature: premium gets everything, while basic only gets standard features. It must then deduct one token from the user quota for standard features and three tokens for premium features, tracking quotas across the list. Return a list of boolean values indicating whether each request was successfully granted based on tier rules and remaining quota.

title: Astronomy constellation identifier
spec: Design `identify(stars)` to analyze a list of observed stars in a night sky segment. Each star is represented by a list containing its horizontal coordinate, vertical coordinate, and brightness magnitude. The logic must filter out any stars with a brightness magnitude less than three. For the remaining bright stars, calculate the straight line distance between every possible pair. Return the total count of valid bright stars and the maximum distance found between any two of them as a list of two numbers.

title: Boarding pass barcode decoder
spec: Write `decode(scans)` to process a list of raw text strings from airport scanners. The logic must slice the string to extract the passenger surname from the first ten characters and the flight number from the next six characters. It must then validate the security signature located at the end of the string by ensuring it contains exactly two numeric digits. Discard any scans with an invalid signature. Return a list of descriptive sentences for the valid scans, such as passenger smith is on flight seven zero two.

title: Recycling center sorting pipeline
spec: Implement `sort(items)` to process a list of scanned trash items. Each item is provided as a list containing its barcode number, a contamination percentage, and its weight. The logic must determine the material category: barcodes starting with one are plastic, two are glass, and three are paper. It must then reject any item with a contamination percentage above fifteen percent. For the accepted items, route them into separate lists for each material category and return a list containing these three categorized lists.

title: Escape velocity calculator
spec: Create `compute(planets)` to evaluate a list of newly discovered exoplanets. Each planet is represented by a list containing its name, its mass relative to earth, and its radius relative to earth. The logic must convert these relative values to calculate the gravitational parameter for each planet. It then computes the required escape velocity using the standard physical formula involving the gravitational parameter and radius. Return a list of sentences formatted with the planet name and its calculated escape velocity rounded to two decimal places.

title: Online exam proctoring flags
spec: Write `monitor(events)` to process a chronological list of actions during a virtual test. Each event is a list containing a timestamp in seconds, the student name, and an action type like out of frame or tab switched. The logic must accumulate penalty points for each student: three points for switching tabs and two points for leaving the webcam frame. It must also check if any single student accumulates more than ten penalty points total. Return a list of student names who have exceeded the ten point threshold and are flagged for review.

title: Geological strata thickness evaluator
spec: Implement `measure(layers)` to analyze core samples from a drilling site. Each layer is provided as a list containing the rock type, the starting depth in meters, and the ending depth in meters. The logic must filter out the initial layer if its rock type is topsoil. For the remaining layers, calculate the absolute thickness by subtracting the starting depth from the ending depth. Identify the single thickest continuous rock layer and return a sentence stating its rock type and total thickness.

title: Meteor shower peak predictor
spec: Design `predict(observations)` to analyze nightly meteor counts over a month. Each observation is a list with the date string, the raw number of meteors seen, and the moon illumination percentage. The logic must normalize the meteor counts by multiplying the raw number by a factor derived from the moon brightness to account for obscured visibility. It then computes a three day moving average of these normalized counts to smooth out weather anomalies. Return the date string that corresponds to the highest moving average value.

title: Virtual pet mood simulator
spec: Write `simulate(actions)` to process a sequence of interactions with a digital companion. Each action is a list containing an activity type like feed, play, or ignore, and a duration in minutes. The logic must update the internal hunger level, decreasing it for feeding but increasing it for playing or ignoring. It must simultaneously update the happiness level, which rises with play but falls rapidly when ignored. Evaluate the final hunger and happiness scores to return a final mood state of ecstatic, content, or unhappy.

title: Typing test speed and accuracy
spec: Create `assess(sessions)` to process the results of multiple user typing tests. Each session is a list containing the total characters typed, the number of incorrect words, and the elapsed time in seconds. The logic must calculate the gross words per minute by dividing the total characters by five and adjusting for the elapsed time. It then determines the net words per minute by subtracting the incorrect words from the gross total. Return a list of the net words per minute for each session rounded to the nearest whole number.

title: Mountain bike suspension tuner
spec: Implement `tune(riders)` to generate personalized shock absorber settings. Each rider is represented by a list containing their name, body weight in pounds, and a riding style of aggressive or smooth. The logic must calculate the baseline air pressure by taking half of the rider weight. It must then adjust the rebound damping clicks: adding two clicks for an aggressive style and subtracting one for a smooth style. Return a list of configuration sentences detailing the rider name, recommended air pressure, and rebound clicks.

title: Historical currency converter
spec: Write `convert(transactions)` to evaluate a list of old financial records. Each transaction is a list containing an amount in old currency, the year it occurred, and a transaction identifier. The logic must look up a base exchange rate multiplier determined by the specific decade of the transaction year. It then calculates the equivalent modern value by applying the decade multiplier to the original amount and adding a standard two percent inflation adjustment per year since the transaction. Return the sum of all modern values across the entire list.

title: Solar panel array optimizer
spec: Design `optimize(roofs)` to plan solar installations for a neighborhood. Each roof is a list containing the total square footage, the number of chimney obstacles, and a shade factor percentage. The logic must calculate the usable roof area by subtracting twenty square feet for every chimney obstacle. It then determines the maximum number of standard fifteen square foot solar panels that can fit in the usable area. Finally, it reduces the expected power output by the shade factor percentage and returns a list of expected kilowatt hours for each roof.

title: Handwriting recognition stroke analyzer
spec: Create `analyze(strokes)` to process digital pen movements on a tablet. Each stroke is a list of coordinate pairs representing the path of the pen. The logic must calculate the bounding box width and height for each stroke to determine its overall size. It must then analyze the coordinate progression to classify the stroke as horizontal, vertical, or diagonal based on which dimension changed the most. Return a list of classification words corresponding to the primary direction of each input stroke.

title: City bus route delay estimator
spec: Implement `estimate(segments)` that processes an array of route parts. Each part is a list containing the distance in miles, the traffic condition as a word like heavy or light, and a boolean for whether it is an express lane. The logic must determine the base travel time assuming an average speed of twenty miles per hour. It then adds a five minute penalty for heavy traffic and subtracts two minutes for express lanes. Process each route part to find its individual estimated time, sum them up, and return the total estimated minutes.

title: Deep sea submarine pressure check
spec: Write `check(dives)` to monitor a series of underwater exploratory missions. Each dive is a list containing the target depth in meters, the hull pressure rating in atmospheres, and the available oxygen supply in hours. The logic must calculate the ambient water pressure, which increases by one atmosphere for every ten meters of depth. It must verify that the ambient pressure does not exceed eighty percent of the hull rating. It also calculates the maximum safe dive duration by leaving a one hour oxygen reserve, returning a list of safe dive hours for compliant dives.

title: Marathon pace band generator
spec: Design `generate(runners)` to create custom race strategies for a group of athletes. Each runner is a list containing their name, their target finish time in minutes, and an elevation profile keyword of flat or hilly. The logic must calculate an even split time for each of the twenty six miles based on the target finish time. For hilly profiles, it adjusts the split times by adding thirty seconds to the first half miles and subtracting thirty seconds from the second half miles. Return a list of formatted sentences detailing the runner name and their adjusted first mile split time.

title: Smart sprinkler water usage
spec: Create `calculate(zones)` to track the water consumption of an automated garden system. Each zone is a list containing the plant type, the sprinkler flow rate in gallons per minute, and a boolean indicating if it rained yesterday. The logic must determine the base watering duration: twenty minutes for lawns and ten minutes for shrubs. If it rained yesterday, the watering duration must be cut in half. Multiply the adjusted duration by the flow rate to find the water used per zone, and return the total sum of gallons used across all zones.

title: Drone swarm formation validator
spec: Write `validate(drones)` to ensure a fleet of aerial vehicles is flying safely. Each drone is a list containing its identification number and its three dimensional coordinates in space. The logic must calculate the geometric center of the entire swarm by averaging all coordinates. It must then check the distance between every possible pair of drones to ensure no two drones are closer than a five meter safety radius. Return the identification numbers of any drones that violate the safety radius, or an empty list if the formation is perfectly safe.

title: Vinyl record grading tool
spec: Implement `grade(records)` to appraise a collection of vintage albums. Each record is a list containing the album name, the number of surface scratches, and a boolean for whether the label is faded. The logic must evaluate the scratch severity: zero scratches is mint, one to three is good, and more than three is poor. It must then downgrade the condition by one step if the label is faded. Return a list of sentences stating the album name and its final adjusted condition grade.

title: Wind chime tone synthesizer
spec: Design `synthesize(chimes)` to simulate the acoustic properties of a decorative chime. Each chime is a list containing its material type like aluminum or wood, and its physical length in centimeters. The logic must calculate the fundamental frequency, which is inversely proportional to the length squared multiplied by a material specific constant. It must then determine the resonance decay rate, which is twice as long for aluminum as it is for wood. Return a list of pairs where each pair contains the calculated frequency and its corresponding decay rate.

title: Laser tag tournament scoring
spec: Write a function `score(matches)` that processes a list of match records. Each match is represented as a plain list containing the player name, number of hits made, number of hits received, and number of base captures. The logic must perform several distinct calculations. First, calculate the base score by multiplying the hits made by ten and subtracting the hits received multiplied by five. Next, compute the capture bonus by multiplying the base captures by fifty. Then, determine the player title: novice for a total score under one hundred, expert for over one thousand, and veteran otherwise. Finally, format a result string combining the player name, total score, and title. Return a list of these formatted strings. Example: for a player with twenty hits, five received, and two captures, the base is one hundred seventy five, the bonus is one hundred, total two hundred seventy five, title veteran.

title: Miniature golf scorecard analyzer
spec: Create a function `analyze(scorecards)` that takes a list of lists, where each inner list contains a player's name followed by their stroke counts for eighteen holes. The standard par for every hole is three. First, calculate the strokes over par for each individual hole. Next, calculate a penalty score where any hole taking more than six strokes adds an extra two penalty points. Then, compute a consistency bonus: subtract five points if no hole took more than four strokes. Compute the final adjusted score by summing the baseline strokes, penalties, and bonuses. Finally, format the output as a sentence stating the player name and their adjusted final score. Return a list of these sentences.

title: Strongman competition scorer
spec: Implement `evaluate(athletes)` which accepts a list of lists. Each inner list has an athlete's name, their truck pull time in seconds, log press weight in kilograms, and atlas stone lift count. You must calculate points for each event separately. Compute the pull points by subtracting the time from sixty, multiplying by ten, and ensuring it does not go below zero. Calculate the press points by multiplying the weight by two. Calculate the stone points by multiplying the lift count by fifty. Compute an endurance bonus by adding twenty points if the pull time was under thirty seconds and the stone count was over five. Sum these values to find the overall strongman score. Return a list of tuples containing the athlete name and their total score.

title: Paintball match statistics
spec: Write `tally(roster)` to process a list of player performance records. Each record is a list with the player name, total eliminations, times eliminated, and flags grabbed. First, calculate the offensive score by multiplying the total eliminations by twenty. Next, calculate the defensive penalty by multiplying the times eliminated by ten. Then, compute the objective points by multiplying the flags grabbed by fifty. Calculate a survival bonus of thirty points if the times eliminated is zero. Combine these values to determine the overall match rating for the player. Finally, return a list of formatted strings, one for each player, detailing their name and final match rating.

title: Hydroelectric dam flow manager
spec: Create `regulate(days)` to manage a list of daily reservoir measurements. Each day is a list containing the daily rainfall in millimeters and the current reservoir level in meters. First, compute the expected inflow volume by multiplying the rainfall by five thousand. Next, determine the required spillway release rate; if the reservoir level exceeds fifty meters, the release rate is the inflow plus ten thousand, otherwise it is just the inflow. Then, calculate the energy generated in megawatt hours by dividing the release rate by five hundred. Finally, compute the safety status: critical if the release rate is over fifty thousand, otherwise normal. Return a list of formatted strings combining daily generated energy and the safety status.

title: Pottery kiln firing schedule
spec: Implement `schedule(batches)` which takes a list of pottery batches. Each batch is a list with a clay type string, piece thickness in centimeters, and target temperature in Celsius. First, compute the ramp up duration in hours by multiplying the thickness by one and a half and adding one hour for every three hundred degrees of target temperature. Next, determine the peak hold time: porcelain requires two hours, stoneware requires one hour, and earthenware requires half an hour. Then, calculate the cool down duration which is exactly half of the ramp up duration. Compute an ambient delay factor of one extra hour if the target temperature exceeds one thousand two hundred degrees. Sum these durations to find the total firing time. Return a list of total hours for each batch.

title: Skateboard street run evaluator
spec: Write `judge(runs)` to score a list of skateboard runs. Each run is a list containing the skater name, base trick difficulty points, maximum rail grind distance in meters, and the number of foot touches on the ground. First, calculate the trick score base by multiplying the difficulty points by two. Next, compute the rail bonus by adding five points for every meter of grind distance above three meters. Then, calculate the landing deductions by subtracting ten points for every foot touch. Compute a flawless run bonus of twenty points if there were zero foot touches. Combine the base, bonus, deductions, and flawless bonus to find the final adjusted score. Return a list of formatted strings with the skater name and their final score.

title: Rock climbing route grader
spec: Create `grade(routes)` to evaluate a list of climbing routes. Each route is a list with the route name, steepness angle in degrees, average handhold size in millimeters, and the total number of rest points. First, calculate the steepness modifier by taking the angle minus ninety, multiplying by two, ensuring it is at least zero. Next, evaluate the hold difficulty by subtracting the hold size from fifty, doubling the result, with a minimum of zero. Then, compute the fatigue reduction by multiplying the rest points by five. Calculate an endurance penalty of ten points if the angle exceeds one hundred and there are no rest points. The overall difficulty score is the steepness modifier plus hold difficulty minus the fatigue reduction plus the penalty. Return a list of tuples with the route name and overall difficulty score.

title: Hot air balloon flight planner
spec: Implement `plan(flights)` which processes a list of planned flights. Each flight is a list containing the total passenger weight in kilograms, ambient air temperature in Celsius, and balloon envelope volume in cubic meters. First, calculate the gross lift capacity by multiplying the volume by a factor of one point two, then adjusting downwards by five percent for every ten degrees above zero Celsius. Next, determine the required propane consumption rate per hour, which is twenty liters plus one liter for every fifty kilograms of passenger weight. Then, compute a cold weather consumption penalty of five extra liters per hour if the temperature is below ten Celsius. Estimate the maximum safe flight duration in hours based on a standard fuel load of one hundred liters divided by the final consumption rate. Return a list of maximum duration estimates.

title: Synchronized swimming routine scorer
spec: Write `score(routines)` to evaluate a list of team performances. Each performance is a list containing the team name, a list of five technical judge scores, a list of five artistic judge scores, and a count of synchronization errors. First, calculate the average technical score by summing all five scores, subtracting the highest and lowest, and dividing by three. Next, calculate the average artistic score using the exact same highest and lowest dropping method. Then, compute the synchronization penalty by multiplying the error count by zero point five. Calculate a perfection bonus of one point if the error count is exactly zero. The final total score is the sum of the two averages minus the penalty plus the bonus. Return a list of tuples with the team name and final score.

title: Firework show choreographer
spec: Create `choreograph(shells)` to process a list of fireworks. Each shell is a list with the shell size in inches, primary color string, and visual effect type string. First, calculate the launch delay interval by multiplying the shell size by one point five seconds. Next, determine the burst altitude by multiplying the size by one hundred feet. Then, compute the safety perimeter radius, which is seventy feet per inch of shell size. Calculate a crowd warning flag: true if the radius exceeds three hundred feet, false otherwise. Finally, format a launch instruction string combining the shell color, effect, altitude, delay, and warning flag. Return a list of these formatted instructions.

title: Sumo wrestling tournament standings
spec: Implement `rank(wrestlers)` that takes a list of competitors. Each wrestler's data is a list with their name, total wins, total losses, and current rank tier number. First, calculate the win percentage by dividing wins by the sum of wins and losses. Next, determine the promotion step factor: if wins exceed losses by at least four, the step is positive one, if losses exceed wins by at least four, the step is negative one, otherwise zero. Then, calculate a dominance bonus of an additional positive one step if the win percentage is above ninety percent. Compute the new rank tier by adding the step factors to the current rank. Return a list of strings stating the wrestler name and their updated rank tier.

title: Bobsled team selector
spec: Write `select(candidates)` to evaluate a list of athlete profiles. Each profile is a list containing the athlete's name, thirty meter sprint time in seconds, push weight in kilograms, and driving experience in years. First, calculate the sprint speed factor by taking five seconds minus the sprint time, multiplying by fifty. Next, calculate the push power index by multiplying the push weight by zero point eight. Then, compute the driving bonus by multiplying the experience years by five. Determine a weight penalty if push weight is under ninety kilograms, subtracting ten points from the total. Determine the overall composite score by summing these metrics. Sort the athletes by their composite score descending and return the names of the top four athletes.

title: Perfume batch formulator
spec: Create `formulate(recipes)` to process a list of fragrance recipes. Each recipe is a list with the scent name, number of top note drops, heart note drops, and base note drops. First, calculate the total oil volume in milliliters by summing all drops and dividing by twenty. Next, determine the required alcohol base volume by multiplying the total oil volume by four to achieve a twenty percent concentration. Then, compute the distilled water addition, which is ten percent of the alcohol volume. Calculate a maturation time in weeks: two weeks if base notes are the majority of the drops, otherwise one week. Return a list of formatted strings detailing the scent name, oil volume, alcohol volume, water volume, and maturation time required for each batch.

title: Miniature wargame army validator
spec: Implement `validate(armies)` which takes a list of army profiles. Each profile is a list with the army name, total unit point cost, number of elite units, and a list of faction keyword strings present. First, check if the total point cost is exactly two thousand to meet the legal tournament size. Next, verify that the elite unit count does not exceed three. Then, determine if the faction mixture is legal by checking if all keyword strings start with the same first letter (acting as a common allegiance). Finally, calculate the deployment rating by multiplying the elite unit count by five. Create a validation report string for each army stating whether it is tournament legal, its errors if any, and its deployment rating. Return a list of these report strings.

title: Karate tournament bracket maker
spec: Write `bracket(fighters)` to categorize a list of participants. Each participant is a list with their name, age in years, weight in kilograms, dojo name, and years of martial arts experience. First, determine the age division: juniors for under eighteen, seniors for eighteen to thirty four, and masters for thirty five and up. Next, calculate the weight class category: lightweight for under seventy kilograms, middleweight for seventy to eighty five, and heavyweight for above eighty five. Then, determine the experience tier: beginner for zero to two years, advanced for more than two years. Generate a full division code string by combining the age division, weight class, and experience tier. Return a list of tuples containing the fighter name and their final division code.

title: Juggling pattern simulator
spec: Create `simulate(patterns)` to evaluate a list of juggling routines. Each routine is a list containing the juggler's name, number of props, height of throws in meters, and a skill rating from one to ten. First, calculate the air time of each throw by taking the square root of the height divided by five, multiplied by two. Next, determine the required hand speed in throws per second by dividing the number of props by the air time. Then, compute a complexity penalty by subtracting two from the hand speed if there are more than five props. Compute the expected number of successful catches before a drop by multiplying the skill rating by twenty and subtracting the adjusted hand speed squared. Return a list of tuples with the juggler name and estimated catch count.

title: Food truck location selector
spec: Implement `select(locations)` to process a list of potential spots. Each spot is a list with the street name, average hourly pedestrian count, number of nearby competitor trucks, and daily parking fee in dollars. First, calculate the base traffic score by dividing the pedestrian count by ten. Next, compute the competitor deduction penalty by multiplying the number of competitors by fifteen. Then, calculate the parking fee cost adjustment by subtracting the fee from fifty, allowing negative values. Determine a high volume bonus score if the pedestrian count is above one thousand, adding twenty points. Determine the final viability score by summing the traffic score, penalty, parking adjustment, and bonus. Return a list of the street names sorted by their viability score from highest to lowest.

title: Surfboard shaping dimensions
spec: Write `shape(surfers)` to calculate custom board specifications. Each surfer profile is a list containing their weight in kilograms, experience level string (beginner, intermediate, advanced), and typical wave height in feet. First, calculate the optimal board volume in liters: multiply weight by zero point nine for beginners, zero point seven for intermediates, and zero point five for advanced. Next, determine the ideal board length in inches by taking the volume, multiplying by one point two, and adding the wave height times two. Then, compute the rocker curve degree by multiplying the wave height by one point five. Compute the fin setup type: thruster if wave height is under five feet, quad if five or over. Return a list of strings detailing volume, length, rocker, and fin type for each surfer.

title: Table tennis paddle assembler
spec: Create `assemble(orders)` to process custom paddle requests. Each order is a list with the customer name, blade wood type (carbon or all-wood), forehand rubber thickness in millimeters, and backhand rubber thickness. First, calculate the blade weight: carbon is eighty five grams, all-wood is seventy five grams. Next, compute the forehand rubber speed rating by multiplying its thickness by forty. Then, calculate the backhand rubber spin rating by multiplying its thickness by thirty five. Calculate the total assembled weight by adding the blade weight and both rubber thicknesses multiplied by ten. Determine the overall paddle balance category: if speed exceeds spin by twenty, it is offensive, if spin exceeds speed, it is defensive, otherwise all-around. Return a list of strings with the customer name, total weight, and balance category.

title: Gymnastics vault evaluator
spec: Implement `score(vaults)` to evaluate a list of competitors. Each gymnast is represented by a list containing their name, a list of five integer judge execution scores, and a base difficulty decimal value. First, calculate the average execution score by summing the five judge scores, dropping the lowest and highest, and dividing by three. Next, compute the raw total by adding the base difficulty to the average execution score. Then, apply a standard neutral deduction penalty if any single judge score was below seven, deducting zero point five from the total. Compute a perfect landing bonus of zero point three if all retained execution scores are ten. Return a list of strings that combine the gymnast name and their final adjusted score.

title: Fencing bout analyzer
spec: Write `analyze(bouts)` to process a list of match results. Each bout is a list containing the fencer's name, touches scored, touches received, number of yellow cards, and number of red cards. First, calculate the touch indicator difference by subtracting touches received from touches scored. Next, determine the penalty point deductions: yellow cards are zero points but red cards cost one point each. Then, calculate a defense bonus of two points if touches received is less than three. Compute the final effective bout score by adding the touch indicator to the penalties (which are negative) and the defense bonus. Finally, format a performance string stating the fencer's name and their effective score. Return a list of these performance strings.

title: Kite buggy race aerodynamic analyzer
spec: Create `analyze(routes)` to evaluate racing lines. Each route is a list with the buggy identifier, distance in kilometers, pilot weight in kilograms, and average wind speed in knots. First, calculate the baseline drag force by multiplying the distance by two and adding the weight times three. Next, compute the wind assistance multiplier: add one to the wind speed divided by fifteen. Then, calculate the required line tension by multiplying the baseline drag by the wind multiplier. Evaluate the structural risk level: high if tension exceeds five hundred, medium if above three hundred, and low otherwise. Return a list of formatted strings with the buggy identifier, required tension, and risk level.

title: Ceramic glaze mixing calculator
spec: Implement `mix(batches)` to calculate parameters for preparing glaze. Each batch is a list containing the base mineral string, water percentage, total dry weight in grams, and ambient studio temperature in Celsius. First, calculate the water volume in milliliters by multiplying the total dry weight by the water percentage divided by one hundred. Next, determine the base mixing time: silica needs fifteen minutes, feldspar twelve, and kaolin ten (default to ten for others). Then, compute the resting time adjustment based on studio temperature: subtract one hour from a standard twenty four hour rest for every degree the room is above twenty Celsius. Calculate an evaporation compensation by adding fifty milliliters to the water volume if the temperature exceeds twenty five degrees. Return a list of formatted strings describing the water volume, mixing time, and resting time for each batch.

title: Scuba dive profile planner
spec: Write `plan(dives)` to evaluate repetitive dive plans. Each dive plan is a list containing the diver's name, planned depth in meters, bottom time in minutes, and an integer representing residual nitrogen from previous dives. First, calculate the current nitrogen absorption score by multiplying the depth by the bottom time and dividing by ten. Next, determine the combined pressure factor by adding the residual nitrogen to the current absorption score. Then, compute the required surface interval time in minutes by multiplying the combined pressure factor by five. Calculate a deep dive penalty adding thirty extra minutes to the surface interval if the planned depth is greater than thirty meters. Return a list of tuples with the diver's name and the total required surface interval time.

title: Tarot Card Reading Generator
spec: Write a function `predict(spread)` that takes a list of strings representing drawn cards and their orientation, such as moon reversed or sun upright. The logic must separate the card name from its orientation. It should assign a base power value of ten to major cards like sun, moon, and star, and five to minor cards like cups or swords. The power is doubled if upright and halved if reversed. Finally, it must categorize the total reading score as either favorable, neutral, or ominous. Return the final total power and the category as an array. For example, an input of ["sun upright", "cups reversed"] returns [22.5, "favorable"].

title: Chariot Racing Dynamics
spec: Write a function `race(chariots)` that takes a list of strings where each string provides a team name, horse speed, and chariot weight separated by commas. The logic must extract these three components and convert the numeric values. It should calculate the base acceleration by dividing the horse speed by the chariot weight. Then, apply a track penalty that reduces the acceleration by ten percent for every fifty pounds of weight over two hundred. Finally, determine the expected lap time by dividing a standard track length of one thousand by the adjusted acceleration. Return a list of arrays containing team names and their expected lap times. For example, an input of ["red team, 100, 250"] returns [["red team", 11.11]].

title: Cyberpunk Hacking Minigame Evaluator
spec: Write a function `hack(nodes)` that accepts a list of hexadecimal strings representing target network nodes. The system must decode each hexadecimal string into its decimal equivalent. It then checks if the decimal value is a prime number, which indicates a secure firewall node. For non-prime nodes, it calculates a vulnerability score by summing the individual digits of the decimal number. If the total vulnerabilities across all nodes exceed fifty, the intrusion is successful. Return an array containing a boolean for success and the count of firewall nodes found. For example, an input of ["0A", "1F", "07"] returns [false, 2].

title: Fantasy Sports Draft Analyzer
spec: Write a function `draft(players)` that processes an array of strings containing player names, their projected points, and their age. The evaluation must parse these details and convert the numbers. It needs to calculate an age penalty, deducting five percent of the projected points for every year the player is over thirty. Next, it must calculate a value over replacement by subtracting a baseline of fifty points from the adjusted projection. Finally, filter out any players with a negative value over replacement and sort the remaining players from highest to lowest value. Return the sorted list of player names. For example, an input of ["smith 100 32", "jones 80 25"] returns ["jones", "smith"].

title: Urban City Zoning Allocator
spec: Write a function `zone(blocks)` that takes an array of numbers representing the population density of city blocks. The logic must categorize each block based on density thresholds. Blocks with a density under one hundred are marked as rural, between one hundred and five hundred as residential, and above five hundred as commercial. It must then calculate the projected tax revenue, applying a flat tax of ten for rural, twenty for residential, and fifty for commercial blocks. Finally, it should compute the city wide average tax revenue per block. Return an array containing the categorized list of block types and the average revenue. For example, given [50, 600], it returns [["rural", "commercial"], 30].

title: Satellite Debris Collision Avoidance
spec: Write a function `navigate(debris)` that receives an array of coordinate arrays representing space junk locations on a two dimensional plane. The module must calculate the Euclidean distance from the satellite origin at zero zero to each piece of debris. It then determines a threat level, classifying distances under ten as critical, under fifty as warning, and otherwise safe. For critical threats, it computes an evasion maneuver vector by inverting the coordinates and scaling them by a factor of two. Return a list of evasion coordinate arrays for all critical threats. For example, given [[3, 4], [100, 100]], it returns [[-6, -8]].

title: Linguistics Phoneme Categorizer
spec: Write a function `analyze(words)` that takes a list of English words. The logic must strip out any non alphabetic characters and convert the text to lowercase. It should count the number of vowels in each word to estimate the syllable count. Next, it evaluates the ratio of consonants to vowels, flagging any word with a ratio greater than three as complex, and others as simple. Finally, it groups the words into two lists based on this complexity flag. Return an array containing the list of simple words followed by the list of complex words. For example, an input of ["a", "rhythms"] returns [["a"], ["rhythms"]].

title: Ghost Hunting Evidence Analyzer
spec: Write a function `investigate(clues)` that accepts a list of strings representing environmental readings like freezing, spikes, or orbs. The logic must count the occurrences of each evidence type. It checks specific combinations to identify paranormal entities, such as requiring both freezing and orbs to identify a phantom, or spikes and freezing to identify a wraith. If the evidence does not match these exact pairs, it defaults to identifying a poltergeist. Next, it computes an activity level based on the total number of clues divided by three. Return an array with the entity name and the activity level. For example, an input of ["freezing", "orbs", "freezing"] returns ["phantom", 1].

title: Artisan Cheese Aging Predictor
spec: Write a function `predict(batches)` that takes a list of strings where each string contains a cheese type, starting moisture percentage, and storage temperature separated by spaces. The system must parse these values and identify the cheese category as hard or soft based on whether the moisture is below forty percent. It calculates the required aging days, multiplying the moisture by the temperature, and then halving the result for soft cheeses. Next, it determines the final expected flavor profile, labeling it sharp if the aging exceeds one hundred days, and mild otherwise. Return a list of flavor profiles for each batch. For example, an input of ["cheddar 30 5"] returns ["sharp"].

title: Ice Hockey Penalty Kill Analyzer
spec: Write a function `evaluate(shifts)` that accepts a list of numbers representing the duration of penalty kill shifts in seconds. The logic must convert each shift duration into a fatigue penalty, adding one fatigue point using integer division for every full ten seconds over forty seconds. It then determines the player injury risk, marking it as high if the fatigue points exceed five, and low otherwise. Finally, it calculates the overall penalty kill efficiency by finding the percentage of shifts that resulted in low injury risk. Return an array containing the list of risk assessments and the overall efficiency percentage. For example, given [45, 120], it returns [["low", "high"], 50].

title: Blacksmith Forging Simulator
spec: Write a function `forge(actions)` that processes a list of action strings such as heat, strike, or quench. The simulation must track a metal temperature and a shape quality, both starting at zero. Heating increases temperature by fifty, striking increases quality by ten but drops temperature by five, and quenching finalizes the process. It must apply a penalty subtracting five from quality if a strike occurs when the temperature is below twenty. Finally, it categorizes the weapon tier based on the final quality, returning masterwork if over fifty, and standard otherwise. Return an array with the weapon tier and the final quality score. For example, given ["heat", "strike", "quench"], it returns ["standard", 10].

title: Stand Up Comedy Set Builder
spec: Write a function `build(jokes)` that takes an array of strings representing joke topics and their estimated laugh duration in seconds. The system must parse the laugh duration and categorize each joke as a quick liner if under five seconds, or a story if longer. It sequences the set by placing all quick liners first to warm up the crowd, followed by the stories. It then calculates the total expected applause time by summing all durations and adding a ten percent bonus if the set contains more than five jokes. Return an array with the sorted list of joke topics and the total expected applause time. For example, ["cats 4", "airplanes 10"] returns [["cats", "airplanes"], 14].

title: Pirate Treasure Map Decoder
spec: Write a function `decode(instructions)` that accepts a list of strings detailing directions, like north five or east ten. The module must parse the direction and the numerical pacing distance. It converts these instructions into Cartesian coordinates, starting from zero zero, adjusting the horizontal and vertical axes accordingly. Next, it calculates the straight line distance from the origin to the final coordinates using the Pythagorean theorem. Finally, it determines the required digging effort by multiplying this final distance by a soil density factor of three. Return an array containing the final horizontal coordinate, the vertical coordinate, and the digging effort. For example, ["north 3", "east 4"] returns [4, 3, 15].

title: Billiards Shot Geometry Analyzer
spec: Write a function `analyze(shots)` that processes a list of numbers representing the incoming angles of billiard balls hitting a cushion. The logic must calculate the reflection angle for each shot, assuming a standard table that perfectly mirrors the angle. It then applies a spin deviation, adding two degrees to angles over forty five, and subtracting one degree from smaller angles. Finally, it flags any resulting angle outside the bounds of zero to ninety degrees as a scratch. Return a list of the adjusted reflection angles, replacing any invalid angles with the word scratch. For example, an input of [30, 100] returns [29, "scratch"].

title: Compost Bin Ratio Balancer
spec: Write a function `balance(materials)` that receives an array of strings representing added materials like leaves, grass, or scraps. The logic must classify each material as carbon rich or nitrogen rich. Leaves and twigs are carbon, while grass and scraps are nitrogen. It tallies the total count of carbon and nitrogen items to compute the carbon to nitrogen ratio. It then evaluates the compost health, declaring it optimal if the ratio is exactly two, too wet if under two, and too dry if over two. Return an array containing the ratio as a decimal and the health status. For example, given ["leaves", "leaves", "grass"], it returns [2.0, "optimal"].

title: Theater Lighting Cue Sequencer
spec: Write a function `sequence(cues)` that takes an array of strings detailing lighting changes, such as red fade or blue snap. The system must parse the color and the transition type. It calculates the transition duration based on the type, assigning five seconds for a fade and zero seconds for a snap. It then checks the power load, assigning a cost of ten for red lights and five for blue lights. Finally, it sums the total duration and the total power load across all cues. Return an array containing the total duration and the total power load. For example, an input of ["red fade", "blue snap"] returns [5, 15].

title: Bonsai Tree Pruning Advisor
spec: Write a function `prune(branches)` that accepts a list of numbers representing the lengths of a bonsai tree branches in centimeters. The logic must calculate the average branch length across the entire tree. It then identifies any branch that is more than fifty percent longer than this average as overgrown. For each overgrown branch, it computes a suggested cut length to bring it exactly down to the average size. Finally, it counts how many branches require no cutting at all. Return an array containing the list of suggested cut lengths and the count of untouched branches. For example, given [10, 10, 25], it returns [[10], 2].

title: Caving Expedition Equipment Planner
spec: Write a function `plan(depths)` that processes an array of numbers representing the depths of vertical drops in a cave system. The module must calculate the required rope length for each drop by adding a safety margin of ten feet to the depth. It determines the number of required anchor bolts by dividing the rope length by twenty and rounding up to the nearest whole number. Next, it sums the total rope length and total bolts required for the entire expedition. Return an array containing the total rope length and the total bolt count. For example, an input of [30, 55] returns [105, 6].

title: Tabletop RPG Loot Generator
spec: Write a function `loot(encounters)` that takes a list of numbers representing the difficulty level of defeated enemies. The system must assign a base gold piece value by multiplying the encounter level by fifty. It then determines if a magic item drops by checking if the level is an even number. For magic drops, it calculates the item rarity tier, assigning uncommon for levels under five, and rare for anything higher. Finally, it totals all the gold and compiles a list of the magic item rarities. Return an array with the total gold and the list of rarities. For example, given [3, 6], it returns [450, ["rare"]].

title: Stained Glass Window Planner
spec: Write a function `design(panels)` that processes an array of strings representing the shape and color of glass pieces, like square blue or triangle red. The logic must parse the shape to calculate the area, assuming squares are ten square inches and triangles are five square inches. It calculates the material cost by applying a multiplier based on color, where blue costs two dollars per inch and red costs three. Finally, it sums the total area and the total cost for the entire window layout. Return an array containing the total area and the total cost. For example, an input of ["square blue", "triangle red"] returns [15, 35].

title: Origami Folding Step Estimator
spec: Write a function `fold(patterns)` that takes an array of strings containing crease instructions like valley double or mountain single. The logic must parse the crease direction and the multiplicity. It calculates the step count by assigning two points for double folds and one point for single folds. It evaluates the structural stress, which increases by five for every mountain fold. Finally, it categorizes the overall difficulty as expert if the total step count exceeds ten or the stress exceeds twenty, and beginner otherwise. Return an array with the total steps and the difficulty category. For example, given ["mountain double", "valley single"], it returns [3, "beginner"].

title: Vintage Clock Repair Estimator
spec: Write a function `repair(gears)` that accepts a list of numbers representing the number of broken teeth on various clock gears. The system must calculate the base repair time, allocating fifteen minutes for each broken tooth. It determines if a gear needs full replacement, which occurs if a gear has more than three broken teeth. For gears needing replacement, it adds a flat manufacturing penalty of one hundred and twenty minutes instead of the per tooth time. Finally, it sums the total repair time across all gears and converts it into hours. Return the total repair time as a decimal number of hours. For example, an input of [1, 4] returns [2.25].

title: Magic Potion Brewing Sequence
spec: Write a function `brew(ingredients)` that takes a list of strings representing magical ingredients and their preparation method, like root crushed or leaf diced. The logic must parse the ingredient name and the action. It computes the base toxicity, assigning a value of ten for roots and five for leaves. It then applies a preparation modifier, reducing the toxicity by half if the item is crushed, but doubling it if diced. Finally, it sums the final toxicity of all items and flags the potion as lethal if the total exceeds twenty, or safe otherwise. Return an array with the total toxicity and the safety flag. For example, an input of ["root crushed", "leaf diced"] returns [15, "safe"].
